newsitem.title: USA: BPA surprises power market with transmission rates.
newsitem.headline: BPA surprises power market with transmission rates.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration's decision Monday to offer separate prices for power generation and transmission beginning with Tuesday's pre-schedulings was unexpected by many market participants.
"They took a lot of people by surprise by breaking out the cost of transmission," said one power marketer. "I think BPA thought they could make a little bit more money this month by starting it now."

Under the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's order on open transmission access, utilities are required to separate generation and transmission prices, as well as operations staff, starting November 1.
"Today is sort of a trial," said a trader at Bonneville, a federal power agency. "I wouldn't be surprised if it changed tomorrow."
For Tuesday pre-schedulings, BPA offered firm, peak-hour power at $21.00, compared with $20.00 for Monday.
But the agency today posted an additional $1.00 per MWh charge for transmissions within the Northwest and $2.27 for deliveries to the California-Oregon and Nevada-Oregon borders.
"I don't think they are going to sell too much at COB at over $23.00," noted one trader. "That $2.27 for COB/NOB is especially surprising."
Bonneville said it raised prices after strong sales over the weekend and for Monday.
"The BPA prices are high if you are looking at purchasing in monthly blocks or for a week or two, but for next-day deals they are not that bad," said another regional trader.
He said scheduling uncertainties heading into a new month were serving to artificially raise prices.
"People are scrambling to settle for October," agreed another trade source.
